Built the full extension. Summary of what's in `/Users/andreacollet/Projects/nabz`:

**Architecture decision** (per your framing): both popup and DevTools panel are supported, sharing one parsing layer (`src/parsers/`) and one DOM renderer (`src/utils/render.ts`) — they only differ in how they *capture* headers:
- **Popup** needs data instantly on icon click (page may have loaded minutes ago) → background service worker using `chrome.webRequest.onResponseStarted` (read-only, no blocking permission), writing to `chrome.storage.session` per tab.
- **DevTools panel** uses `chrome.devtools.network` instead, which needs zero extra permissions and naturally gives per-navigation history (capped at 25 entries, panel-local).

**Permissions**: just `webRequest`, `storage`, and `host_permissions` for `http(s)://*/*` (not `<all_urls>`). README §2 explains why each is needed and why an `activeTab`-only refetch design was rejected (it'd duplicate the request and could report different edge/cache data than the real navigation).

**Parsers** (`src/parsers/`) are pure functions with no `chrome.*` dependency — `serverTiming.ts`, `cloudflare.ts`, `shopify.ts`, `generic.ts` (Fastly/Akamai/CloudFront/Vercel/Netlify), combined by `index.ts` into the normalized `InfrastructureInfo`. 33 vitest unit tests cover them, including a case built from your exact popup mockup example.

**Verified working**: `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (33/33 pass), and `npm run build` all succeed; `dist/` is a complete, loadable unpacked extension (manifest + bundled JS + HTML/CSS all cross-reference correctly).

I removed one thing I'd initially added (a `fieldMeta.ts` label/provenance registry) after building the UI, because the popup mockup's labels are context-specific per section (e.g. "PoP" in the Cloudflare block vs "Edge location" in Overview for the same underlying field) — hand-curating labels directly in `render.ts` covered that better than a generic path→label map ever did, and the map ended up unused.

README covers all 7 requested sections including how to test against a live Shopify/Cloudflare storefront. Nothing is committed to git — let me know if you'd like that done.
